messages:
maria.g: Heads up — since ~08:12 we've got ~120 small training pods Pending in us-west2. They're 0.25 GPU slices and the scheduler keeps saying 'No fit' across a bunch of nodes. CA isn't adding new nodes in us-west2b even though us-west2a has room.

kai: Can you paste the Describe output for one of the pending pods?

maria.g: paste below from a representative pod:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age                 From               Message
  ----     ------            ----                ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x45 over 13m)  default-scheduler  0/48 nodes are available: 48 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu (or fragmented slots), 12 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
Pod spec excerpt:
```
resources:
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25
nodeSelector:
  gpu-type: a100-v2
```

aj: That Insufficient message + the taint is the combo. We recently enabled nodepool anti-affinity across AZs for balance; CA's `balance-similar-node-groups` is preventing scaling in 2b because 2a has under-utilized nodes but with fragmented slots.

sasha: Fragmentation is the real issue: our nodes are 8x slices (4 slots of 0.25) but long-running services have consumed non-contiguous slices leaving 0.25 holes that the plugin doesn't coalesce. Scheduler treats them as not-fittable because we pack by whole-slot.

kai: Do we have metrics on slice occupancy? Which nodepools are affected?

maria.g: A quick query from prometheus shows a cluster-level slot utilization of 72% but 37% of nodes report at least 1 completely free slot while the rest have 0.25-0.5 unusable fragments. Nodepools: gpu-west2-a (45 nodes), gpu-west2-b (30 nodes), gpu-west2-c (25 nodes). Pending queue is concentrated in west2-b.

aj: CA log snippet from the scaling loop (09:05):
```
I0926 09:05:12 cluster_autoscaler.go:123] No scale up: nodegroup gpu-west2-b matches balance policy; similar nodegroups available in other AZs
I0926 09:05:12 cluster_autoscaler.go:125] Candidates: []*NodeGroup{gpu-west2-a (capacityAvailable: 2), gpu-west2-b (capacityAvailable: 0)}
```

kai: So CA thinks there is available capacity in another AZ and refuses to scale group b, but scheduler can't fit because of fragmentation. CA's decision is correct given its view but wrong for our packability constraints.

sasha: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily set `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` so CA can scale b, 2) drain/defragment a couple nodes (evict small batch jobs) to create contiguous slots, 3) tweak scheduler predicate to prefer nodes with contiguous free slots, or 4) change binpacking policy to prefer consolidating small slices.

maria.g: Also cost tradeoff: scaling b up adds 10 nodes (wasteful if 2a could absorb). But draining + compacting will cause small pod churn and some preemptions. Which do we want today?

aj: For short term, flip balance flag for 30m and watch. That should let CA add at least 3 nodes to b and drain backlog. For medium term: we should implement a probe that computes fragmentation per node and feed it to CA (or a scheduler plugin).

kai: I can toggle the CA flag if oncall approves. @sasha @maria.g thoughts? :thinking:

sasha: +1 to toggle for the next 1h and then revert. Also add an alert so we don't leave it off. I'll open a short-lived playbook.

maria.g: Approved. If kai can flip it now, we'll monitor pending count and node allocation.

kai: Doing it now. Command I ran:
```
kubectl -n kube-system set args deploy/cluster-autoscaler --container=cluster-autoscaler -- --balance-similar-node-groups=false
```
Waiting for rollout...

infra-bot: [09:18] cluster-autoscaler deployment restarted by kai. New args: --balance-similar-node-groups=false

maria.g: Within 4 minutes CA proposed 3 nodes for gpu-west2-b and started provisioning. Pending decreased from 120 -> 18. :thumbsup:

aj: Nice. Followups:
- schedule a small RFC to add a fragmentation metric and a scheduler heuristic
- consider node labeling to prefer compaction (e.g., pack=true) and a defrag controller to cordon/evict low-priority small jobs overnight
- evaluate whether our device plugin can expose slot-level allocatable to kube-scheduler

kai: I'll revert the flag in 1h and post an incident note in #incidents summarizing what we did.

sasha: Filed a short ticket: INFRA-3145 (defrag probe + CA hook). Assigning to aj for design.

maria.g: Thanks everyone. We'll keep an eye on costs post-scale. Logged the anomaly under the cost center for batch workloads.

infra-bot: [10:20] Alert resolved: Pending GPU pods in cluster us-west2 back to normal.
